title: Behavioral Economics of AI: LLM Biases and Corrections

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM decisions using classic cognitive psychology prompts (e.g., Kahneman and Tversky lotteries) and experimental economics tasks to detect deviations from Expected Utility Theory, including loss aversion, probability weighting, ambiguity aversion, and hyperbolic discounting.

Testing LLMs with probabilistic reasoning questions and time-series forecasting scenarios to measure deviations from Bayesian updating and rational expectations, including base rate neglect, sample size neglect, the gambler's fallacy, confirmation bias, anchoring, and overconfidence.
